records.finding: Assumptions 3.1-3.4 and Theorem 3.1 bind sparse-group prediction bounds to moments, tau-mixing decay, population restricted eigenvalues, effective sparsity and a dependence/tail-sensitive penalty. The manuscript keeps its own stronger learning construction distinct and does not infer arbitrary population nuisance rates or score inference from this empirical prediction bound.

Section 2.1 uses a joint-density-weighted positive normal operator. Assumptions A.1-A.5 and Theorem 4.1 support the displayed integrated squared-error rate for iid bounded-support observations, density and coefficient smoothness, eigenvalue decay and appropriate regularization. The manuscript explicitly separates this operator and exponent from its singular-value sequence example, Lebesgue loss from population loss, and the series method's stronger diagonality; no confidence band or dependent-bank inference is inferred.

Definition 1 and Lemma 2 require exponential domination by nonnegative supermartingales and measurable mixtures. Proposition 5 yields the displayed two-sided normal-mixture boundary with l0=1. The manuscript reconstructs its bounded-score sufficient law and simultaneous-in-time guarantee, while distinguishing variance-adaptive alternatives and ordinary fixed-time normal intervals.

Equations (5)-(8) derive a null-centered significance band under the zero-response hypothesis, lead-lag exogeneity and a long-run score covariance; the joint construction uses Bonferroni. Both manuscript contexts correctly distinguish this from a general response confidence band and withhold growing-horizon simultaneous coverage without accumulated-error control.

Theorems 1-2 distinguish identified common-trend contributions from individually normalized trends and impose the stronger loading-estimation rate for stationary differences of the latter. The manuscript uses this to retain rotation/normalization uncertainty; giving a filtered state an economic name does not identify its intervention.

Section 2 contrasts separate horizon regressions with VAR propagation restrictions after identification. Sections 6.1-6.3 distinguish overlapping projection errors from score dependence and explain lag augmentation under strong innovation restrictions. The manuscript preserves that separation and does not transfer the source uniformity claim to arbitrary nonlinear LPs, learned instruments or unrestricted panels.

Assumption 1 requires innovation mean independence from all other dates; Definition 1 restricts the VAR root class. Assumptions 2-3 add eighth moments, summable innovation-product cumulants and scaled-design nonsingularity. Proposition 1 gives marginal uniform normality with h/T tending to zero near unit roots. The manuscript's fixed four-horizon Bonferroni construction is identified separately and its external-IV family is not conflated with this reduced-form AR target.

Section 2 specifies the customer information, transition/shock factorization, known discount and shock law. The affine payoff inversion on page 7 and counterfactual identification condition in Theorem 1 confirm that observationally equivalent historical payoffs need not produce the same changed-transition counterfactual. The manuscript labels its logit normalization and constructive example rather than claiming arbitrary payoff recovery.

Assumptions 1-3 and Theorem 1 express identification as nested regressions under sequential exogeneity, sufficient recorded history and positivity. Section 4 recursively introduces Riesz corrections with existence conditions. The single manuscript context appropriately connects this nested-functional view to its own fixed-stochastic-policy projection derivation, without treating that connection as an automatic guarantee for unrestricted learned policies.

Assumptions 1-2 and Lemma 1 establish continuous linear targets and projected representers; Corollary 2 gives nonlinear sensitivity factors with representer variation not bounded by one. The archived Theorem 2 signed difference disagrees with its Appendix B.4 expansion. The manuscript explicitly records and corrects that source sign inconsistency using the displayed orthogonal decomposition, while preserving the valid squared bound and overlap/moment restrictions.

Condition LP-IV and equation (8) require relevance plus contemporaneous and lead-lag exclusions; controls must establish the residualized conditions. Sections 2.4-2.5 separate score long-run variance, normalization and response identification from historical-shock/variance recovery. Section 3's proxy-SVAR adds invertibility and common VAR dynamics. All five manuscript contexts preserve these distinctions, including persistent instrument measurement noise and the need for changed normalization for news shocks.

Assumptions 1-3, Theorem 1 and Lemma 1 use sequential proxy restrictions, bridge existence and latent completeness to identify compatible-history joint counterfactual quantities and the associated two-stage regime. The source explicitly separates existence from uniqueness and allows nonunique observable solutions. The manuscript does not extend the result to every cross-world law or infer an integrable solution from injectivity alone.
